editorial:
Imagine you are cruising through space on a giant cargo ship when you pick up a weird signal. That is how things kick off here. You meet a crew that finds a mutated saxophone player who has been floating in the void for two decades. He looks pretty strange, but he is actually a sweetheart who just wants to play some music and find love with a pretty journalist on board. It feels like a wacky mix of a space trip and a romantic comedy, giving you a cozy but odd vibe as the characters bond in the middle of nowhere.

What really makes this work is how the mood shifts when two bad guys hijack the ship. The action picks up quickly, and seeing a mutant fight off criminals is honestly a blast. While some of the special effects look a bit old, the charm and humor make up for it. You should definitely check this out if you love weird 80s sci-fi. If you can, try adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best colors, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the mutant uses his strange powers and his saxophone to outsmart the criminals. He saves the journalist and the rest of the crew in a big final fight. The bad guys get kicked off the ship, and the mutant finally finds a place where he belongs. It wraps up with a sweet moment showing that being different is okay, and he gets to stay with the people who love him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s space movies and oddball characters
